item.strong: SRS v1 · Digital Customer Onboarding System (OT-based e-KYC & V-CIP)

srs.title: Digital Customer Onboarding System (OT-based e-KYC & V-CIP)
srs.summary: This system enables remote customer onboarding for banks and registered entities (REs) using Video KYC (V-CIP) and Offline Aadhaar Verification (OTP/manual entry). It enforces strict RBI regulatory limits on deposit balance (₹1 Lakh), annual credit limits (₹2 Lakh), and term loan limits (₹60,000) to
assumptions: The system relies on real-time connectivity to the Unified Aadhaar Foundation and CKYCR APIs for authentication and retrieval of KYC records.
Customer consents for OTP-based authentication are provided digitally and verifiably within the user interface before initiating the verification flow.
The 'Central Negative List' data feeds are available and updated in near real-time via the integration gateway.
stakeholders: Registration Entity (RE): The bank or non-banking financial institution using the system.
Customer: The end-user initiating the account opening request and providing KYC data.
Regulator (RBI): The oversight body whose circulars drive the compliance rules (referenced in evidence).
CKYCR (Central Know Your Customer Repository): The external data repository from which KYC records are pulled.
Aadhaar Authority: The external authority providing the OTP and identity verification services.

Aadhaar Offline Verification Constraints (Evidence E5, Question 3): The user selected 'Manual OTP entry by Customer' (Option A). However, Evidence E5, paragraph i) states this applies when 'offline',

risks.title: Regulatory Non-Compliance on Age Limits
risks.text: The requirement to perform a 'Fresh KYC' when a user turns 18 (User Answer Q2, Option A) contradicts the regulatory stance. Evidence E2, paragraph (ii), states that a 'fresh photograph shall be taken'

openIssues: Scope of Negative List Integration: The user opted for 'Central Negative List only', which may be too restrictive if internal bank blacklists or other government sanctions lists are mandated by specific business units or local regulations not covered in the provided evidence.

Periodic KYC Workflow for Minors: The system logic for handling the transition from Minor to Adult (Fresh Photo vs. Fresh Full KYC) needs clarification against Evidence E2, paragraph (ii) to ensure the correct data points (photo, address, CDD docs) are flagged for automation.

Mobile Number Change Policy: The system must enforce strict due diligence when changing mobile numbers (Evidence E4, paragraph 59), but the implementation logic for detecting 'change' and triggering the 'robust process' is not detailed in the user answers.

requirements.statement: The system shall support remote account opening exclusively via Video KYC (V-CIP), prohibiting all-branch onboarding flows for new remote customers.
requirements.acceptance: The onboarding module allows initiation of a V-CIP flow for a new customer; no options exist to select 'Branch Visit' for initial remote account opening.

requirements.statement: The system shall automatically trigger a Fresh KYC workflow when a customer's date of birth indicates they have reached the age of 18.
requirements.acceptance: Upon a customer's birthday, if their age turns 18, the system generates a high-priority task for the Relationship Executive to perform Fresh KYC.

requirements.statement: For offline Aadhaar verification during V-CIP, the system shall implement a 'Manual OTP Entry' function where the customer enters the OTP provided by the bank officer, rather than auto-fetching or XML
requirements.acceptance: In the offline verification flow, the UI presents an input field for the 6-digit OTP for the customer to enter manually; automatic scanning or XML upload paths are disabled.

requirements.statement: The system shall cross-reference customer details against the Central Negative List and flag accounts for rejection if a match is found.
requirements.acceptance: The negative list screening module queries the Central Negative List and returns a 'Reject' status for any customer with a matching identifier, blocking further account opening.

requirements.statement: The system shall validate liveness during the video interaction by analyzing interaction variance to ensure real-time engagement.
requirements.acceptance: The video processing engine rejects the session if liveness detection metrics fall below the required threshold, indicating a pre-recorded interaction.

requirements.statement: The system shall reject the account opening process immediately if the customer provides any prompt responses at the end of the video interaction.
requirements.acceptance: The system analyzes the transcript/audio of the V-CIP session; if 'prompting observed' triggers are detected, the process is terminated and the application marked as rejected.

requirements.statement: The system shall validate that the customer being on-boarded via V-CIP is either a 'New' customer or a 'Case Rejected Earlier' status, factoring this into the workflow logic.
requirements.acceptance: The system checks customer status against 'Existing', 'New', and 'Previously Rejected' states; it allows V-CIP initiation only for 'New' or 'Previously Rejected' categories.

requirements.statement: The system shall redact or blackout the customer's Aadhaar number in all stored records and logs.
requirements.acceptance: A report containing customer KYC data shows the Aadhaar number field replaced by asterisks or a masked value, containing zero visible digits of the original number.

requirements.statement: The system shall block any deposit account opened via OTP-based e-KYC if the account age exceeds one year without subsequent face-to-face identification.
requirements.acceptance: The system monitors account maturity; for any OTP-based e-KYC deposit account, an automated hold action is applied after 365 days if the customer has not completed face-to-face ID.

requirements.statement: The system shall calculate and enforce a strict credit limit of Rs. 60,000 for term loans for accounts opened using OTP-based e-KYC.
requirements.acceptance: When processing a term loan application for an OTP-based e-KYC account, the system calculates the aggregate sanctioned amount; if the sum exceeds Rs. 60,000 in a financial year, it
